summary: Mardu Swanepoel identifies four patterns common among leading AI agents, framing the analysis through Picasso's idea of "stealing" as deep study and adaptation rather than copying. The first pattern, focus modes, constrains the agent's action and input space into specialized modes such as planning or debug, allowing engineers to optimize output quality on a smaller surface area while aligning user expectations. Cursor exemplifies this with dropdown-selectable modes: a planning mode that produces no code and only asks questions, and a debug mode with a hypothesis-driven approach using a dedicated debug server. The second pattern, transparent execution, shifts the user-agent relationship from delegation to collaboration by surfacing reasoning, tool calls, and their inputs and outputs. This builds trust and enables early intervention to reduce wasted work. Claude co-work displays a live task list alongside all tool call inputs and outputs; Manifold similarly shows task progress and what the agent reviewed. The third pattern, personalization, aims to increase the agent's speed to understanding—not merely speed to outcome—by embedding the user's own methods, knowledge, and principles. Harvey's playbooks encode a legal firm's contract review methods so the agent replicates the firm's approach. Harvey and Claude also use memory, skills, and connectors to deepen personalization. The fourth pattern, reversibility, lets users undo agent actions at various granularities, bounding the downside cost of mistakes and encouraging users to assign higher-value, riskier tasks. Cursor supports rollback at line, file, and conversation levels and can run multiple model outputs in parallel from the same input. Harvey integrates with Microsoft Word's native API to present changes as a reviewer or editor would natively see in Word.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction: Picasso's "Steal" as Deep Study
sections.summary: Swanepoel opens with Picasso's quote about stealing, clarifying it means deeply studying, understanding, and adapting something to create something better. He introduces the plan to study four leading agents and extract four patterns, covering for each what it entails, the value it adds, and real-world implementation.

sections.title: Pattern 1: Focus Modes
sections.summary: Focus modes constrain the agent's action and input space into specific modes like planning or research. Benefits include improved output quality on a smaller surface for engineers and aligned user expectations. Cursor demonstrates this with dropdown-selectable modes: planning mode produces no code and asks questions; debug mode uses a hypothesis-driven approach with a dedicated debug server and logs.

sections.title: Pattern 2: Transparent Execution
sections.summary: Transparent execution shifts from delegation to collaboration by making agent reasoning, tool calls, and their inputs and outputs visible. This builds trust in outputs and enables early intervention to reduce waste. Claude co-work shows a task/to-do list and all tool call inputs and outputs. Manifold similarly displays task progress and what the agent reviewed.

sections.title: Pattern 3: Personalization
sections.summary: Personalization embeds the user's thoughts, systems, knowledge, and principles into the agent to optimize for speed to understanding rather than just speed to outcome. Harvey uses playbooks encoding a legal firm's contract review methods and creates memories over time. Claude offers skills, connectors, and system integrations to extend personalization.

sections.title: Pattern 4: Reversibility
sections.summary: Reversibility lets users undo agent actions, bounding the cost of mistakes and making the ROI calculation easier, which encourages bolder, higher-value task delegation. Cursor supports rollback at line, file, and conversation levels and can run multiple model outputs in parallel from the same input. Harvey's Word add-in integrates with the native Word API to present changes as a reviewer or editor would natively see.

sections.title: Closing
sections.summary: Swanepoel thanks the audience, acknowledges covering a lot in a short time, and invites further questions.
